stem:
A student performs an experiment on tracing the path of a ray of light passing through a rectangular glass slab for different values of angle of incidence. He fixes pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\), while looking through the face DC, so that their feet are in line with the images of the feet of the pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\):

(The figure shows a rectangular glass slab ABCD with face AB on top and DC at the bottom. An incident ray with pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) strikes the top face AB; the emergent ray with pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\) leaves from the bottom face DC.)

options.label: A
options.text: neither the feet nor the heads of the images of pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\) are in line with the feet and heads, respectively, of pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).

options.label: B
options.text: only the heads of the images of pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\) are in line with the heads of pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).

options.label: C
options.text: feet, as well as the heads of the images of pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\) are in line with the feet and heads respectively of pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).

options.label: D
options.text: only the feet of the images of pins \(P_3\) and \(P_4\) are in line with the feet of pins \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).

(The figure shows parallel rays from a far-off object striking the device X on the right; the reflected rays converge to a sharp image on a screen standing on the SAME side as the incoming rays, i.e. in front of X.)

The device X is a:

A student, while doing the experiment, on tracing the path of a ray of light passing through a rectangular glass slab, measured the three angles marked as \(\theta_1\), \(\theta_2\) and \(\theta_3\) in the figure. His measurements could be correct if he were to find:

(The figure shows a rectangular glass slab. \(\theta_1\) is the angle of incidence at the top face between the incident ray and the normal; \(\theta_2\) is the angle the refracted ray makes with the normal inside the slab; \(\theta_3\) is the angle the ray makes with the normal at the bottom face where it leaves the slab.)

Four students A, B, C, and D carried out measurement of the focal length of a concave mirror as shown in the following four diagrams. The best result will be obtained by the student:

(In each diagram a distant tree sends rays to a concave mirror which reflects them onto a screen. In A and B the incoming rays are not truly parallel and the convergence is poor. In C the parallel rays converge low on the screen. In D the incoming rays are clearly parallel and converge to a single sharp point on a correctly placed screen.)

The D (protractor) used for measuring the angle of incidence (i) and the angle of reflection (r), has to be positioned in the ways illustrated in figures (W), (X), (Y) and (Z). The figures show: (W) protractor with its straight (diameter) edge laid along the mirror surface, near the incident ray; (X) protractor with its straight edge laid along the normal, near the incident ray; (Y) protractor with its straight edge laid along the mirror surface, near the reflected ray; (Z) protractor with its straight edge laid along the normal, near the reflected ray. For angle of incidence and for angle of reflection respectively, the correct positions are:

As light IM is incident on the surface PQ, as shown, the emergent ray has to be:

(The figure shows a rectangular glass slab with top face PQ and bottom face YX. The incident ray IM strikes the top face PQ at M and is refracted to N on the bottom face. From N several candidate emergent rays are drawn, labelled D (shallow, up-right toward X), C (down-right), B (steeper down-right) and A (almost vertically down).)

The figure shows a ray of light as it travels from medium A to medium B. Refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A is:

(The boundary between medium A, below, and medium B, above, is horizontal with a vertical normal. The ray in medium A makes 30 degrees with the surface, i.e. 60 degrees with the normal; the refracted ray in medium B makes 45 degrees with the normal.)

A beam of light is incident through the holes on side A and emerges out of the holes on the other face of the box as shown in the Figure. Which of the following could be inside the box?

(The figure shows a box. A set of parallel rays enters through evenly spaced holes on the left face A. On the right face the rays emerge from a single region and fan out, i.e. the parallel beam has been converged to a point and then diverges.)

On regular reflection from the surface XY, the reflected ray will go along:

(The surface XY is horizontal with a vertical normal at the point of incidence. The incident ray arrives from the upper-left making an angle i with the normal. On the right of the normal four candidate reflected rays are drawn: A (steepest, nearest the normal, at angle i/3), B (next, at angle i/2), D (shallower) and C (almost along the surface XY).)

While performing the experiment on tracing the path of a ray of light passing through a glass slab as shown in the given diagram, four students interpreted the results as given below. Which one of the four interpretations in correct?

(The figure shows a rectangular glass slab. The angle of incidence at the top face is marked i, the angle of refraction inside the slab is marked r, and the angle of emergence at the bottom face is marked e.)

A light ray enters from medium A to medium B as shown in Figure. The refractive index of medium B relative to A will be:

(The horizontal boundary separates medium A, below, from medium B, above, with a vertical normal. In medium A the ray is nearly along the surface, i.e. it makes a large angle with the normal; in medium B the ray is steeper, i.e. it makes a smaller angle with the normal, so the ray bends toward the normal on entering B.)

The path of a ray of light coming from air passing through a rectangular glass slab traced by four students are shown as A, B, C, and D in Figure. Which one of them is correct? In A the ray passes straight through the slab without bending. In B the ray bends towards the normal on entering, travels through, and bends away from the normal on leaving so that the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (laterally shifted). In C the ray passes straight through without bending. In D the ray bends on entering but the emergent ray is not parallel to the incident ray.

The correct sequencing of angle of incidence, angle of emergence, angle of refraction and lateral displacement shown in the following diagram by digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:

(The figure shows a ray through a rectangular glass slab. The angle at the top face between the incident ray and the normal is marked 2; the angle of the refracted ray to the normal inside the slab is marked 4; the angle at the bottom face between the emergent ray and the normal is marked 1; and the perpendicular gap between the emergent ray and the undeviated continuation of the incident ray is marked 3.)

Which of the following ray diagrams is correct for the ray of light incident on a concave mirror as shown in figure? The incident ray is parallel to the principal axis (C and F are marked on the axis, P is the pole). In (a) the reflected ray passes through the focus F. In (b) the reflected ray passes through the centre of curvature (2F). In (c) the ray is reflected straight back along the same path. In (d) the reflected ray crosses the axis between the focus F and the pole P.

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (a) - reflected ray passes through the focus F

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (b) - reflected ray passes through the centre of curvature

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (c) - ray reflected back along itself

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (d) - reflected ray crosses the axis between F and P

stem:
The figure given alongside shows the image of a clock as seen in a plane mirror. The correct time is:

(In the mirror image the hour hand points to the right, towards roughly the 3 o'clock position, and the minute hand points to the lower-left, towards roughly the 7 (35-minute) position, so the image appears to read about 2:35.)

A student traces the path of a ray of light passing through a rectangular glass slab for three different values of the angle of incidence (namely 30 degree, 45 degree, 60 degree). He produces the incident ray and measures the perpendicular distance, l, between the produced incident ray and the emergent ray. He will observe that:

options.label: A
options.text: l keeps on increasing with increase in angle of incidence

options.label: B
options.text: l keeps on decreasing with increase in angle of incidence

options.label: C
options.text: l remains the same for all three angles of incidence

options.label: D
options.text: l is maximum for \(i=45^\circ\) and is less than this value both for \(i=30^\circ\) and \(i=60^\circ\)

stem:
The focal length of the concave mirror in the experimental set up, shown below, equals:

(On a metre scale, the concave mirror stand is placed at about the 15.5-16 cm mark and the screen stand, where the parallel rays from a distant object converge to a sharp image, is placed at about the 4.5 cm mark.)

Select from the following the best experimental set-up for tracing the path of a ray of light passing through a rectangular glass slab. Four set-ups P, Q, R and S are shown, each with two pins fixed on the incident ray. In P the ray is almost normal to the slab (very small angle of incidence) with the two pins close together. In Q the ray strikes at a moderate oblique angle (about 45 degrees) with the two pins well separated. In R the ray is oblique but the two pins are close together. In S the ray strikes at a large (near-grazing) angle with the pins separated.

Out of the four rays I, II, III and IV shown to fall on the concave mirror, the incorrect one is:

(The figure shows a concave mirror with F and C marked on the principal axis. Rays I, II and IV are drawn parallel to the principal axis striking the mirror, and ray III is drawn passing through the centre of curvature C. Their reflected rays are also shown.)

A student obtains a sharp image of the distant window (W) of the school laboratory on the screen (S) using the given concave mirror (M) to determine its focal length. Which of the following distance should he measure to get the focal length of the mirror?

Beams of light are incident through the holes A and B and emerge out of the holes C and D respectively as shown in the figure. Which of the following could be inside the box?

(The figure shows a box. Two parallel beams enter through holes A (top) and B (bottom) on the left face and emerge through holes C (top) and D (bottom) on the right face at the same heights, parallel and undeviated.)

Which of the following ray diagrams is correct for the ray of light incident on a lens shown in figure? The incident ray comes from the upper-left and passes through the focus F on the object (near) side before reaching a convex lens (optical centre O). In (a) the emergent ray is reflected straight back. In (b) the emergent ray goes upward, diverging away from the axis. In (c) the ray passes straight through the optical centre undeviated. In (d) the emergent ray travels parallel to the principal axis.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (c) - ray passes straight through the optical centre

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (d) - emergent ray parallel to the principal axis

stem:
The value of n for the incident ray through air medium is:

(The figure shows a ray passing from air, above, into a medium of refractive index n, below, across a horizontal boundary with a vertical normal. The incident ray in air makes a small angle of incidence i with the normal, while the refracted ray in the medium bends away from the normal, making a larger angle of refraction r, so the ray bends away from the normal on entering the medium.)

Parallel rays, from a distant tree, incident on the device X, form its distinct image on a screen as shown in the diagram. The diagram correctly showing the image of the tree on the screen is: In diagram A the parallel rays pass through device X and converge to a sharp, inverted image of the tree on a screen placed on the far side of X (opposite the incoming rays). In diagram B the rays pass through X but the tree image shown on the far-side screen is upright (erect).

options.text: A and the device X is a concave mirror

options.label: B
options.text: A and the device X is a convex lens

options.label: C
options.text: B and the device X is a convex lens

options.label: D

stem: Match the following with the correct response: (1) A perpendicular drawn at the point of incidence to the reflecting surface (2) The rays which strike the mirror surface near the periphery (3) The ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (4) The ratio of speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in a medium. Responses: (A) Linear magnification (B) Normal (C) Absolute refractive index (D) Marginal ray.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Mirror formula (2) Lens formula (3) Magnification (4) Focal length. Responses: (A) \(\frac{R}{2}\) (B) \(\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\) (C) \(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\) (D) \(-\frac{v}{u}\).

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Pole (2) Principal axis (3) Radius of curvature (4) Aperture. Responses: (A) The midpoint of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror (B) The radius of the hollow sphere of which the reflecting surface forms a part (C) The imaginary straight line joining the pole and the centre of curvature (D) The width of the mirror from which reflection can take place.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Plane mirror (2) Concave mirror (3) Convex lens (4) Convex mirror. Responses: (A) Virtual image, inverted and large (B) Virtual image, erect and same size (C) Virtual image, positive focal length (D) Real image, negative focal length, negative power.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Highest refractive index (2) Lowest refractive index (3) Head lights of a car (4) Side rear view of a mirror. Responses: (A) Convex mirror (B) Ice (C) Diamond (D) Concave mirror.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Refraction (2) Reflection (3) Rarer medium (4) Denser medium. Responses: (A) Bending of light (B) Velocity of light increases (C) Bouncing back of light (D) Velocity of light decreases.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Convex lens (2) Concave lens (3) Concave mirror (4) Convex mirror. Responses: (A) Diverging (B) Virtual image smaller than object (C) Virtual image larger than object (D) Converging.

Match the following with the correct response: (1) Concave mirror (2) Convex mirror (3) Focal length (4) Lateral inversion. Responses: (A) A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards (B) Objects actually to the left appear to be on the right in the image (C) The distance between the pole (P) and the focal point (D) A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inwards.
When a lemon kept in water in a bowl is viewed from outside, it appears _______ than its actual size.
The radius of curvature of a concave mirror is 30 cm. The focal length of the mirror will be _______ cm.
Magnification produced by a rear-view mirror fitted in vehicles is:

In an experiment to determine the focal length of a convex lens, a student obtained the image of a distant window on the screen. To determine the focal length of the lens, she should measure the distance between the _______.

For the experiment on finding the focal length of a convex lens by obtaining the image of a distant object, a laboratory assistant keeps the following apparatus on the table: 1. A stand with a metal needle fixed in it. 2. A stand with the given convex lens fitted in it. 3. A thick cardboard white screen. 4. A metre scale. A student can do the experiment by using the apparatus listed as (here A, B, C, D refer to items 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively):
A student obtains a sharp inverted image of a distant tree on a screen behind a convex lens. She then removes the screen and looks through the lens in the direction of the object. She will see:

options.label: A
options.text: an inverted image of the tree at the focus of the lens

options.label: B
options.text: an erect image of the tree on the lens

options.label: C
options.text: a blurred image on the wall of the laboratory

options.label: D
options.text: no image as the screen has been removed

stem: A student carries out the experiment of tracing the path of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab for two different values of angle of incidence (\(\angle i=30^\circ\) and \(\angle i=45^\circ\)). The set of values of the angle of refraction (\(\angle r\)) and angle of emergence (\(\angle e\)) likely to be observed in the two cases are:

While performing an experiment on determining the focal length of a convex lens, a student obtains a sharp inverted image of the laboratory window on the screen and measures the distance between the screen and the lens. The student then repeats the experiment taking a distant tree as the object in the second case. In order to get a sharp image of the tree on the screen, the student now needs to hold the screen:

options.label: D
options.text: slightly farther away from the lens
